:::{#exr-loglik-iid}
#### Log-likelihood of an independent sample

For mutually independent data $\dsn{X}$,
use @thm-lik-iid
to write the [log-likelihood](#def-loglik) $\llik(\param)$
as a sum over the observations.
What does each term become
if the $\Rvar_\iobs$ also share a common distribution $\p(X = x \mid \param)$?
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-loglik-iid}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\llik(\param)
&\eqdef \log{\Lik(\param)}
&& \text{(definition of log-likelihood)}\\
&= \log{\prodin \p(\Rvar_\iobs = \rvar_\iobs \mid \param)}
&& \text{(likelihood of an independent sample)}\\
&= \sumin \log{\p(\Rvar_\iobs = \rvar_\iobs \mid \param)}
&& \text{(log of a product is a sum of logs)}
\end{aligned}
$$

With a common distribution,

$$
\p(\Rvar_\iobs = \rvar_\iobs \mid \param) = \p(X = \rvar_\iobs \mid \param),
$$

so each term is $\log{\p(X = \rvar_\iobs \mid \param)}$.

:::
